headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the full costs of their dedicated grid infrastructure and capacity, aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocacy groups, residential ratepayers, Governor Spanberger.
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry.
news_headline: Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission has ordered data centers to pay for all required transmission infrastructure they exclusively use, a move Governor Spanberger says will save civilians 'hundreds of millions of dollars.' This action aims to prevent future electricity price increases for average Virginians, which have seen a 76% hike largely due to the massive power demand from the state's 570+ data centers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and aiding state water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (potentially due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will increase transparency on data center water usage in Virginia by requiring waterworks operators to categorize monthly sales data, including usage by data centers. This bill, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap for water supply planning, especially during droughts, despite information on specific facilities remaining protected as trade secrets.

headline: Data Centers: Site Assessment, Sound Profile Required
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for new high-energy data centers, focusing on noise impacts on residential areas and schools, and potential effects on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near potential data center sites, environmental and conservation groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations.
news_headline: Data centers; site assessment, sound profile of the high energy use facility.
news_summary: HB153, now law, boosts transparency in data center development by requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to request information on potential impacts to water quality, agriculture, forests, and parks. This legislation also mandates disclosure of costly utility infrastructure needs, such as transmission lines and substations, for high-energy-use facilities (100 MW or more).
